en: Points of Controversy Great Fifty-Section Third Chapter
The Discourse on the Knowledge of Rebirth According to Deeds:
Is the knowledge of rebirth according to deeds the divine eye? Yes.
And does he attend to those who have gone according to their karma, and see forms with the divine eye?
One should not say so… [and so on] … Does he attend to those who have gone according to their karma, and see forms with the divine eye?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then do two contacts and two consciousnesses coincide?
You should not say so …pe… .
Is the knowledge of the destiny of beings according to their karma the divine eye? Yes.
One attends thus: "These worthy beings," and one attends thus: "endowed with misconduct of body."
He reflects: "They are possessed of verbal misconduct," and he reflects: "They are possessed of mental misconduct," and he reflects:
"They are revilers of the noble ones," and he reflects: "They hold wrong views," and he reflects:
"They have undertaken actions based on wrong views. When their bodies break up...
He attends to the thought: "After death, they have been reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, even in hell";
he attends to the thought: "But these worthy beings"; he attends to the thought: "They were endowed with good conduct of body";
he attends to the thought: "They were endowed with good conduct of speech"; he attends to the thought: "They were endowed with good conduct of mind."
And does he attend to them thus: "They do not revile the noble ones," and does he attend to them thus: "They possess right view," and does he attend to them thus:
"They undertake actions based on right view," and does he attend to them thus:
"With the breakup of the body, after death, they have reappeared in a happy destination, in a heavenly world," while seeing forms with the divine eye?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … One attends to the thought,
“With the breakup of the body, after death, they have reappeared in a happy destination, a heavenly world,” and one sees forms with the divine eye? Yes.
Is there a conjunction of two contacts and two consciousnesses?
One should not say so… [as before]… Is the knowledge of the destiny of beings according to their deeds the divine eye?
"Yes.
"Is there anyone who, though not possessing the divine eye, and having neither attained nor realized it, knows how beings fare according to their karma?
"Yes."

If there is someone with the divine eye who, without having obtained, attained, or realized it, knows beings according to their destination in accordance with their karma, then indeed, sir, you should not say:

"The knowledge of beings according to their destination in accordance with their karma is the divine eye. Is the knowledge of beings according to their destination in accordance with their karma the divine eye?
"Yes.
"Does the Venerable Sāriputta know the knowledge of how beings fare according to their karma?
"Yes."
If the Venerable Sāriputta knows the knowledge of how beings fare according to their kamma,
then surely it should not be said that "the knowledge of how beings fare according to their kamma is the divine eye.
Is the knowledge of how beings fare according to their kamma the divine eye?
“Yes.
“Does the Venerable Sāriputta know the knowledge of how beings fare according to their karma?
“Yes.”
“Does the Venerable Sāriputta possess the divine eye?
“One should not say so…” [and so on].
“Does the Venerable Sāriputta possess the divine eye?”
“Yes, [he did].
“Did not the Venerable Sāriputta say this:
‘Neither for the sake of recollecting past lives...’?”
Nor of the divine eye;
nor of the supernormal power of reading the minds of others,
nor of the purification of the ear-element.
"At death and at rebirth,
no aspiration exists for me"—
is this indeed a sutta?
“Yes, [it is so].
Therefore, it should not be said:
“The knowledge that reaches according to karma is the divine eye.”
The discussion on the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings according to their kamma is finished.
